mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the individual's country of citizenship (e.g., HM Passport Office for UK nationals)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary, then Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; consular legalization only if the country of origin is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed utility provider or regulated financial institution in the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified notarial copy followed by Hague Apostille where the original document is issued in a non-English language or a non-Common Law jurisdiction; notarized certification suffices for UK-issued documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed directors, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list, the EU consolidated sanctions list, and Gibraltar's domestic designations under the Sanctions Act 2019. Enhanced due diligence is compulsory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates; PEP status remains applicable for at least 12 months after leaving public office, or indefinitely for high-risk exposures. Screening must be refreshed at least every 90 days and immediately prior to any material corporate event or banking relationship establishment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House e-Services (online registry portal of the Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar, HM Government of Gibraltar)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory working language of the register is English. Every proposed company name must use Latin-alphabet characters only; a non-English name must be accompanied by a certified English transliteration approved by the Registrar. The name must end with the word 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or 'Public Limited Company'/'PLC' for public companies) and must be distinguishable — not identical and not confusingly similar — to any existing name on the register. Reserved or protected words may be used only with the prior consent of the Registrar or the relevant functional authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of a rejection notice, the applicant may submit a written request for reasons and a request for reconsideration, attaching revised name tokens or evidence of ministerial consent for sensitive words; the Registrar must issue a written decision within 14 days. If the Registrar upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for judicial review of the administrative decision within 21 days of the final decision. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately reserve a new name without prejudice. Any third party may object to an already granted name within 12 months of registration on grounds of identity or confusing similarity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for the proposed low-risk, unlicensed electric cargo e-bike manufacturing entity, provided that a physical Gibraltar registered office address (not a P.O. Box) is maintained by a licensed corporate service provider, the address appears on all corporate stationery, and all statutory registers and accounting records are held at or made available from that address. Actual manufacturing operations are expected to occur in a designated industrial facility outside Gibraltar or in a third-country toll-manufacturing arrangement. The GFSC would require a substantive physical trading office only if the company later applies for a regulated financial services license, an exemption certificate engagement, or a taxable distribution/service-center substance profile.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated low risk of approximately 5-10% of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first three years, given the unlicensed, low-risk manufacturing classification. The probability increases to approximately 20-35% if the company subsequently registers as a Gibraltar distribution and service center under the Economic Substance (Companies and Foreign Companies) Regulations 2019, applies for a Gibraltar VAT or distribution license, or engages in cross-border intra-group financing or intellectual property holding.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981 (as amended), ss. 4-17 and s. 30 (formation, name and exempted-company declaration); s. 99 (registered office); read with the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 and the Exchange Control Act 1972. For recognition in Gibraltar: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (as amended), Part 21 (External Companies) and Parts 2-3 (corporate governance duties).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda (eCompanies online portal); for the Gibraltar external registration: Companies Registry, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, Europort Avenue, Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association, Form D (Declaration of Compliance), Notice of Registered Office, Consents of the First Directors, and Application for Exemption under the Companies Act 1981; followed by Form 1 External Company filing under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Bermuda exempted company. One ordinary share of USD 1.00 (or BMD 1.00) must be issued and fully or partly paid to the founding subscriber; no escrow account or capital-blocking requirement is imposed. Authorised capital is typically USD 12,000 to cap the flat incorporation fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED THAT: (1) the incorporation of the Company under the Bermuda Companies Act 1981 is ratified and the Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws are adopted; (2) the allotment of one fully paid ordinary share to the founding subscriber is confirmed and recorded in the Register of Members; (3) the registered office is established at Canon's Court, 22 Victoria Street, Hamilton, Bermuda; (4) [Director A] is appointed Director and [Secretary B] is appointed Company Secretary; (5) the Directors are authorised to register the Company as an external company in Gibraltar, to open corporate bank accounts, and to engage legal, tax and accounting advisers for the accomplishment of the Company's industrial licensing objectives.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda — eCompanies Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name-reservation request for two ranked proposed names of the exempted company (the second name is a fallback) through the eCompanies portal. The Registrar will reject any name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company or that contravenes s. 30 of the Companies Act 1981 (undesirable names, sovereign or governmental connotations). The name must end with 'Limited'. Reservation confirmation is normally returned within two business days; no notarisation or apostille is required at this pre-filing stage.
required_dossiers: Application for Name Reservation (online form)
Ranked list of proposed names (primary and one fallback)
Copy of payment receipt for the reservation fee (BMD 45)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the primary name is refused on availability or s. 30 grounds, the Registrar automatically considers the fallback name; if both are refused, a fresh application may be submitted free of resubmission charges, and the applicant may appeal the refusal to the Minister of Finance under s. 31 of the Companies Act 1981.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding subscriber (a licensed Bermuda corporate-services provider acting as authorised agent) and the first directors; no government filing at this step.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws using the Bermuda exempted-company template, incorporating the exempted-company declaration required by s. 4(2) of the Companies Act 1981 (intention that the company shall not carry on business in Bermuda other than in furtherance of its business outside Bermuda). The Bye-Laws cover share classes (single ordinary class), board powers, director indemnity, and written-resolution mechanics. The memorandum and bye-laws are executed by at least one subscriber (or two where the client requires a justifiable two-subscriber structure) before an attesting witness; the subscriber is the authorised agent's nominee share trustee to permit immediate online formation.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum of Association (s. 5, Companies Act 1981)
Draft Bye-Laws (s. 11, Companies Act 1981)
Executed Consent to Act as Director (each first director)
Letter of engagement and KYC pack of the authorised corporate-services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If drafting counsel or the Registrar identifies drafting defects (e.g., missing exempted-company declaration or inconsistent authorised-share-number clauses), the defective text is amended and re-executed by the subscriber by a supplementary manuscript amendment; no re-payment of government fees is triggered unless the authorised capital is increased beyond USD 12,000.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda (eCompanies portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically: executed Memorandum of Association, Form D (Declaration of Compliance), Notice of Registered Office, Consents to Act of the first directors, and the request designating the company as an exempted company. Pay the Registrar's incorporation fee of USD 1,735 (authorised capital up to USD 12,000). Upon statutory compliance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation stating the company's name, number, and date of incorporation; corporate existence commences on that date. The authorised agent then obtains the certified copy of the Certificate and prepares the share certificate for the founding subscriber.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum of Association (scanned original)
Form D — Declaration of Compliance
Notice of Registered Office (s. 99)
Consents to Act of the first directors
Payment instruction for USD 1,735 incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or query, the authorised agent must cure the stated defect within 5 business days (amendment, re-execution or clarification); the processing clock is suspended from the query date until the cure is filed. Failure to cure within the statutory period permits the Registrar to refuse the application, in which case the authorised agent lodges a fresh application under the fallback name without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Certificate and Designation of Non-Resident Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Minister of Finance, Government of Bermuda (applications filed through the authorised corporate-services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the application for a Tax Exemption Certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, together with a request to classify the company as non-resident under the Exchange Control Act 1972. The certificate confers an irrevocable statutory guarantee that, should Bermuda ever impose tax on profits, income, dividends or capital gains, the exempted company will be exempt until the protected 50-year period from the date of incorporation has elapsed (and may be extended). The application must declare that the company is beneficially owned by non-Bermudian persons and will not carry on business in Bermuda unless licensed otherwise.
required_dossiers: Form of Application for Tax Exemption Certificate
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Declaration of non-Bermudian beneficial ownership and control
Summary business plan for the electric cargo bicycle OEM manufacturing and European distribution activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Commissioner requires further beneficial-ownership particulars, the authorised agent files the supplementary declarations within 10 business days; a deemed approval flows at the end of the statutory processing window unless a specific requisition is raised, which may be addressed by a solicitor's letter of explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration as an External Company in Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC), Europort Avenue, Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 (External Company) under Part 21 of the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, together with certified copies of the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum of Association and Bye-Laws (English-document originals require no translation; they must be certified by a Bermuda notary and apostilled under the Hague Convention), a notice of the Gibraltar registered address, particulars of directors and company secretary, and the consent of a Gibraltar-resident authorised representative for the service of process. Pay the registration fee of approximately GBP 130. The GFSC Registry then issues a Certificate of Registration as an External Company, conferring full legal capacity to hold assets, contract, and employ staff in Gibraltar.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — External Company registration
Certified and apostilled copy of Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation
Certified and apostilled copy of Memorandum and Bye-Laws
Notice of Gibraltar registered office (street address in Gibraltar)
Consent to act as authorised representative (Gibraltar resident)
Register of directors and secretary (power of attorney sealed by Bermuda counsel)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the GFSC Registry queries the authenticity or completeness of the certified dossiers, the authorised agent resubmits true certified copies (with a corrected apostille) within 10 business days. Registry fee credits are retained if the resubmission occurs in the same application round; otherwise a new Form 1 filing is made with a covering statement referencing the earlier application number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance, Beneficial Ownership Filing and Bank or EMI Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, GFSC (Beneficial Ownership Secure Search system); a Gibraltar-licensed bank or electronic money institution (EMI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial-ownership particulars (PSCs) with the GFSC BOSS system within 14 days of external-company registration. Convene the first board meeting, or pass unanimous written resolutions, to: approve the share certificate issue; adopt the Gibraltar operations plan (OEM sub-contracting, quality control, warehousing and distribution); designate the registered office and authorised representative; and authorise opening of the corporate settlement account with a Gibraltar-licensed bank or EMI. Submit the KYC pack (certified incorporation documents, board resolution, source of wealth, and the AML low-risk assessment appropriate to the Micro_Mobility_OEM commercial model) to support the Swift_LC and TT_Wire payment rails.
required_dossiers: PSC / beneficial-ownership BOSS filing confirmation
First board meeting minutes or written resolutions
Certified copies of incorporation and external-company registration certificates
Bank/EMI account application with KYC and AML questionnaires
Invoices or pro-forma purchase orders evidencing trade-flow purpose (e-bike components and finished units)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or EMI demands enhanced due diligence because the manufacturing business involves physical inventory, provide the industrial-licensing status report, a drafts of letters of credit, and a 12-month cash-flow projection sourced from verified OEM contracts; a further 10-business-day review period is typically granted before a decision is reached.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DEHCC), HM Government of Gibraltar, in coordination with the Development and Planning Commission (building control) and the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Light Manufacturing Operating Permit and Factory Registration under the Environmental Protection Act 2014 (Gibraltar) and the Safety at Work Act 2014 (Gibraltar); a separate financial or sectoral licence is not required (requires_statutory_license = false), but the physical assembly, battery-integrating and warehousing facility requires the following operating clearances.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DEHCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — EIA Screening/Registration tier: no full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required for light assembly of electric cargo bicycles (ISIC 3091) provided installed capacity is below 50,000 units per year, the site area is less than 1 hectare, and the activity is not within a protected zone; a Preliminary Environmental Screening Report and an Operator Pollution Prevention Plan must nevertheless be registered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: zero process discharge to ground or marine waters; only treated sanitary effluent may connect to the public sewer under the Gibraltar Water Pollution Regulations. Air emissions: VOC emissions from the coating and bonding line must meet Best Available Techniques (BAT) benchmark values (e.g., below 30 mg C/Nm3 for abated waste-gas outlets); particulate matter below 50 µg/m3 for any controlled stack. Hazardous waste: lithium-ion battery cells, defective cells and battery-pack waste must be segregated, stored in fire-rated cabinets, and removed by a licensed waste carrier under the Waste (Batteries) Regulations 2011 (Gibraltar); a hazardous-waste consignment note is required for each collection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service confirming means of escape, emergency lighting, and active suppression (sprinkler or gaseous extinguishant) in the battery-charging and storage areas with a lithium-ion fire risk assessment; Building Occupancy and Structural Load Clearance from the Building Control Authority of the Development and Planning Commission confirming floor-load capacity for the assembly line and battery racks; Workplace Occupational Safety Clearance from the Health and Safety Inspectorate under the Safety at Work Act 2014 covering electrical installation certification, 8-hour noise exposure below 85 dB(A), local exhaust ventilation for the coating station, personal protective equipment programme, and a road-test safety zone plan for step-through scooters and cargo bicycles.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, HM Government of Gibraltar (Income Tax Office); online portal: Gibraltar Taxation e-Services (www.gibraltar.gov.gi/taxation)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Bermuda Exempted Company (foreign entity) establishing a presence in Gibraltar: (1) register as an oversea company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies (Companies House) within one month of establishing a place of business; (2) within 30 days of commencing trade, submit Form TR-1 (Taxpayer Registration) to the Income Tax Office, enclosing certified certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, register of directors and shareholders, registered office confirmation and a Gibraltar tax agent authorisation; (3) obtain the Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN), which is the statutory TIN for all corporate tax filings, customs declarations and EU/OECD exchange-of-information purposes; (4) for offshore tax status, file the Qualifying Company application under s.24A of the Income Tax Act 2010, supported by a substance statement; approval is conditional on non-resident beneficial ownership, absence of trading with Gibraltar-resident persons, and continued compliance with the Economic Substance requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — non-resident offshore exempted company; chargeable to Gibraltar income tax on a territorial basis only (income arising in or derived from Gibraltar); foreign-source trading profits are exempt upon Qualifying Company (s.24A) approval; no capital gains tax, no inheritance tax, no wealth tax and no withholding tax on dividends, interest or royalties paid to non-residents.
statutory_election_mechanisms: Qualifying Company election (s.24A, Income Tax Act 2010) — irrevocable election for full exemption of foreign-source income; requires non-resident beneficial ownership, no trade with Gibraltar-resident persons, and satisfactory economic substance in Gibraltar.

Participation exemption election — election to exempt qualifying dividends and capital gains arising from a 10% or greater shareholding in a non-resident subsidiary that is subject to a tax of at least 12.5% in its state of residence (anti-hybrid aligned).

Hybrid mismatch alignment election under the Income Tax (Hybrid Mismatch Rules) — optional election to align the Gibraltar tax classification of the entity with that of the counterparty jurisdiction in order to neutralise deduction-without-inclusion outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Purchase Tax (import consumption duty) — Gibraltar is outside the EU VAT area and applies no VAT, GST or general sales tax. Purchase Tax under the Purchase Tax Act is levied at importation on a closed list of designated goods (alcohol, tobacco, petroleum, motor vehicles and specified luxuries). Electric cargo bicycles, e-bike components and manufacturing inputs are not listed and are outside the scope of the tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no turnover-based registration threshold. The importer must be registered with HM Customs Gibraltar and must file an import entry/declaration for each consignment; Purchase Tax is a transaction-based levy arising on each importation regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — Gibraltar imposes no electronic invoicing mandate, no real-time fiscal clearance API and no digital stamping. Invoices must comply with Income Tax Act record-keeping rules (six-year retention). Customs declarations are processed through the Gibraltar Integrated Tariff system on a pre-clearance/post-clearance model; no machine-readable invoice clearance is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exemption equivalent to zero-rating applies because Gibraltar levies no VAT. (a) Goods manufactured in Gibraltar (the cargo e-bikes) and exported outside Gibraltar are outside the scope of Purchase Tax, provided physical export is evidenced and the goods are not diverted to local consumption; (b) imported goods re-exported within three months qualify for Purchase Tax relief under customs warehousing/transit procedures. Sales to the UK and EU are third-country exports: the foreign buyer accounts for import VAT or reverse charge in the destination state, and the Gibraltar seller retains transport, customs and payment documentation as the condition of exemption.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — Gibraltar Customs export entry (Integrated Tariff / C88 equivalent) containing the unique consignment reference and the exporter TRN.
Bill of Lading (original set, consigned to the foreign buyer) or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from Gibraltar and delivery at destination.

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank SWIFT MT103 credit advice or foreign-exchange repatriation certificate retained in the economic-substance and transfer-pricing file (not a statutory customs condition in Gibraltar, but required as evidence of commercial reality for the s.24A exemption).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HM Customs Gibraltar and the Income Tax Office jointly audit export substantiation and Qualifying Company files. Deficient or fraudulent export evidence triggers assessment of Purchase Tax as if the goods had been consumed locally, with interest from the date of importation; penalties of treble the duty or GBP 500 (whichever is greater), forfeiture of goods and criminal liability (imprisonment up to two years) apply to deliberate misdeclaration. Qualifying Company abuse (trading with Gibraltar residents without Commissioner approval, or failure of economic substance) causes retrospective revocation of the s.24A exemption, assessment on worldwide profits at 12.5% for up to six years, late-payment interest and penalties up to 100% of the tax.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the statutory regulator and licensing authority in Gibraltar for credit institutions, investment firms, insurers and payment-service providers. Gibraltar has no independent central bank; the currency, the Gibraltar pound (GIP), is issued by the Commissioner of Currency (Government of Gibraltar) under the Currency Notes Act 1934 as sterling-linked notes (GIP 1 = GBP 1, fully backed by Bank of England sterling reserve holdings). Monetary stability derives from the Bank of England because GIP is pegged at par to GBP and sterling is legal tender in Gibraltar; the GFSC carries out prudential supervision of Gibraltar-licensed banks pursuant to the Financial Services Act 2019 and the Banking Act 2017, with no exchange-control restrictions. Because the UK Exchange Control Act 1947 is permanently suspended, the GFSC exercises no currency-rationing, no capital-repatriation approval and no FX-transaction registration function.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. GIP is freely convertible into GBP at 1:1 (no margin, no quota) and into EUR/USD through the bank's own FX desk; there is no statutory limit on foreign-currency account balances, no import/export licensing for funds, and no withholding tax on dividend, interest, royalty or management-fee payments remitted by a Gibraltar company to its Bermuda parent. Profit-remittance hurdles are limited to accounting and tax formalities: (i) the company must file audited annual financial statements and a tax return, or an Economic Substance return under the Economic Substance (Companies and Partnerships) Act 2020 where the company is tax-resident; (ii) dividends declared must comply with the Companies Act 2014 solvency test; and (iii) the remitting bank will ask for a board resolution declaring the dividend, a FATCA/CRS self-certification, and confirmation that no Gibraltar tax deduction is required because Gibraltar levies no withholding tax on outbound dividends. Capital-account injections from Bermuda are free of prior approval but are subject to post-fact compliance screening by the receiving bank for source-of-funds evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Gibraltar maintains no export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory time window for the repatriation of export receipts. Proceeds from EU, UK and third-country sales of electric cargo bicycles (HS 8711.60) may be retained indefinitely in any currency in a GFSC-licensed bank account. The only reporting duties of a Gibraltar exporter are: (i) annual economic substance and tax reporting to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office; (ii) Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit (GFIU) suspicious-transaction reports under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 for high-value or unusual trade-payment patterns; and (iii) UK/Gibraltar Common Foreign Security Policy (CFSP) sanctions screening of all counterparties and their banks. Documentary evidence of each export sale (commercial invoice, packing list, proof of dispatch, ocean/air waybill) must be retained for six years to satisfy GFSC conduct rules and any trade-finance audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Multi-Currency Current Account (GIP, GBP, EUR, USD)
Operational Current Account with Trade-Finance Sub-Limit (SWIFT LC Issuance)
Operational Current Account / EUR-Denominated Collection Account
Trade-Finance Desk Account / LC Confirmation and Forfaiting Facility
Private-Banking Treasury Account / Capital Escrow Overlay

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: RESTRICTED-MEDIUM. UK FCA-authorised e-money institutions (Wise Plc, Revolut Ltd) can on-board a Gibraltar-registered corporate for payroll, operating expenses and corporate cards, but cannot lawfully hold the capital escrow or serve as the primary settlement rail because (i) post-Brexit, the UK-EMI cross-border licence does not passport into Gibraltar; the EMI must rely on reverse solicitation or obtain its own GFSC E-Money licence under the Financial Services Act 2019; (ii) Gibraltar banks' own AML rules treat a CDD package built only on an EMI-issued IBAN as materially weaker; and (iii) trade-centric counterparties (LC advising banks in China and India, EU distributors) reject payment orders that do not arrive as SWIFT MT103 from a BIC-identified credit institution. Recommended use: expense cards and payroll under GBP 10,000 per transaction. Prohibited use: LC cover, supplier down payments above GBP 25,000, tax payments, and the Capital Escrow Account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto in-branch attendance is mandated by all tier-1 Gibraltar banks. No Gibraltar regulation explicitly compels physical attendance in every case, but GFSC supervisory practice expects the bank to verify the identity and authority of at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) face-to-face. Remote opening is permitted with (i) apostilled board resolutions appointing signatories, (ii) certified passport copies, (iii) a three-month source-of-wealth statement, and (iv) an online notarised verification call, but remote-only accounts are typically capped at GBP 25,000 per transaction for the first six months and cannot be used for LC issuance until a director visits the branch. Recommended mandate: for a Bermuda-exempt parent, ensure that at least one Gibraltar-resident director attends the in-person interview and signs the wet-ink bank mandate; the Bermuda parent's UBO may appear by video link.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with an opaque ownership chain, including nominee shareholding arrangements, legacy bearer-share structures, or an absence of Gibraltar economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) certified register of members and directors of the Bermuda exempted company under the Companies Act 1981; (ii) Gibraltar register of persons with significant control (PSC) under the Companies Act 2014, s.13; (iii) GFSC economic-substance self-assessment (Form ES) evidencing Gibraltar office, employees and expenditure; (iv) an AML onboarding questionnaire signed by the UBO; and (v) a letter of awareness from the Gibraltar registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection exceeding GBP 200,000 from Bermuda routed through an intermediary non-Gibraltar account, raising source-of-funds concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) notarised and apostilled board resolution authorising the capital increase or contribution; (ii) twelve-month bank statements of the Bermuda parent demonstrating legitimate source of funds; (iii) a source-of-wealth statement with receipts from any crypto-position exit by the UBO; (iv) executed equity subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; and (v) an undertaking that the capital will remain in the Gibraltar entity for at least twelve months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade corridor screening: battery cells procured from the People's Republic of China, motors from India, power semiconductors from Taiwan, and potential sanctions exposure to Russia, Belarus or Iran.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (i) standard commercial invoices, packing lists, insurance certificates and an Incoterms 2020 master contract; (ii) HS 8711.60 dual-use export-control self-classification confirming no military end-use; (iii) end-user and end-use certificates from suppliers; (iv) the bank's enhanced due-diligence questionnaire on sanctioned counterparties; and (v) a signed letter confirming no Russian, Belarusian or Iranian nexus in the supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Turnover-to-capital mismatch: an early-stage manufacturer projects high turnover but holds a small capital base, creating an anomalous cash-flow pattern for the bank's portfolio team.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present (i) board-approved three-year financial projections and a cash-flow plan for the electric-cargo-e-bike product line; (ii) EU and UK distributor purchase orders and supplier contracts; (iii) brand trademark registrations and patent filings for the e-bike platform; and (iv) a transaction-profile forecast covering average invoice size, country distribution and expected frequency of LC issuance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Crypto treasury linkage: the Bermuda parent or UBO historically used digital-asset wallets, creating AML and reputational flags during bank underwriting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) a complete withdrawal trail from exchange statements (e.g., Coinbase, Gemini, or any UK-FCA-registered exchange) to the bank through a licensed custodian or brokerage; (ii) crypto-to-fiat exit statements and relevant tax filings; (iii) a written treasury policy prohibiting crypto wallets for trade settlement and LC collateral; and (iv) consent for the bank to conduct periodic wallet screening of the UBO's public addresses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route: SWIFT MT103 from the Bermuda parent's account at its correspondent bank (e.g., HSBC Bermuda Ltd or Butterfield Bank Bermuda) to the Gibraltar operating company's account at the tier-1 Gibraltar bank. Field guidance: 32A currency and amount (GBP, EUR or USD); 50K ordering customer as the Bermuda Exempted Company; 57A receiving bank BIC; 59 beneficiary as the Gibraltar OpCo; 70 Remittance Information '/INV/ T0100 INTRAGROUP EQUITY CONTRIBUTION - BOARD RESOLUTION [DATE]'. The Gibraltar bank will apply the Bank of England balance-of-payments purpose code T0100 (transfers between related enterprises / inward direct investment) for the UK ECM statistical return. Verification package: (i) board resolution of the Gibraltar entity approving the issuance of shares or loan capital; (ii) signed capital-contribution or shareholder-loan agreement; (iii) FATCA/CRS self-certification showing the Gibraltar tax residence of the receiving entity; (iv) GFSC close-links notification where the injection changes the Gibraltar entity's balance sheet by more than 20%; and (v) source-of-wealth statement for the Bermuda parent. The funds must be classified as share premium (equity) or intercompany loan in the Gibraltar statutory accounts. No GFSC or Bank of England prior approval is required; settlement is T+0 via the receiving bank's London nostro (CHAPS or Faster Payments) or T+1 via TARGET2 for EUR.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the micro-mobility OEM: (1)SWIFT MT103 direct customer credit transfers for low-value supplier and logistics settlements (batteries from Shenzhen, motors from India) with purpose code T0200 (imports of goods) and the full commercial invoice reference in field 70; (2)irrevocable documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by the Gibraltar bank for high-value component purchases above USD 50,000, with an advising or confirming bank in the supplier's country (e.g., Bank of China, ICBC Shanghai, HDFC Mumbai), payable at sight or 90 days; (3)SWIFT MT202 COV bank-to-bank cover payments using the issuing bank's nostro account to match the LC reimbursement terms; and (4)collection-based settlements such as Documents against Payment (SWIFT MT400) as an interim rail before supplier LC limits are established. All outbound payments must be screened against the UK Sanctions List, the OFAC SDN List, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction flags; finished e-bikes have no dual-use restriction, but lithium-ion battery cells require DG-classification paperwork. Settlement is T+0 in GBP via CHAPS, T+1 in EUR via TARGET2, and T+1 in USD via the bank's New York correspondent.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable FX forwards (tenor up to 24 months) in GBP, EUR and USD - permitted under the Financial Services Act 2019 for a Gibraltar-incorporated manufacturer; execution requires a board-approved treasury limit and no exchange-control certificate because GIP/GBP is pegged 1:1 and freely convertible.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) on intercompany or bank-funded EUR, USD and GBP debt lines - permitted; the bank executes under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a GFSC-licensed counterparty and monthly mark-to-market valuations are provided.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing offshore CNY, INR or VND - permitted as a hedge for genuine component-import exposure from Shenzhen, Bangalore and Ho Chi Minh City suppliers; booked with a GFSC-licensed broker or the bank's London desk; NDFs cannot reference GIP/GBP (no NDF market exists) and speculative positions are prohibited under the GFSC Suitability Rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation or an elected alternative date permitted by the Gibraltar Companies Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a GBP 50 default penalty, rising to GBP 500 if overdue for three months; continued default for six months triggers a Registrar's notice and eventual administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Confirmation / Nil Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Gibraltar Income Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the financial year-end; a nil tax return is filed annually to support the tax-exempt zone status of the Bermuda Exempted Company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the due date may lead to a default assessment, interest charges, and late-filing penalties under the Gibraltar Tax Administration Act; persistent non-filing can jeopardise the exempt status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commissioner of Income Tax, Gibraltar Income Tax Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of each accounting period; manufacturing and assembly of electric cargo bicycles is treated as a relevant activity for economic substance filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inadequate substance documentation attracts a fixed GBP 500 penalty and, for prolonged non-compliance, up to GBP 2,000 plus potential adjustment to taxable status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar Companies Registry (Central Beneficial Ownership Database)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the Annual Return; any share transfer or UBO change must be notified to the database within 28 days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or file the register of beneficial owners is an offence exposing directors to fines up to GBP 10,000 and disqualification; default also blocks issuance of certificates of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements (where audit threshold is exceeded or exempt status requires audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies and Commissioner of Income Tax, Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the accounting reference date, filed together with the Annual Return and Corporation Tax Confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delayed or omitted filing attracts civil penalties, adverse audit opinions, and disqualification risk; repeated default may lead the Registrar to apply for a court-backed strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, a mandatory independent audit applies when a company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: annual turnover greater than GBP 10.2 million, balance sheet total greater than GBP 5.1 million, or average number of employees greater than 50. A Bermuda Exempted Company in the electric cargo bicycle manufacturing sector may also be required to file audited financial statements as a condition of maintaining its exempt tax status, regardless of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements for Gibraltar-incorporated entities must be prepared under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); qualifying smaller entities may elect IFRS for SMEs. Tax-exempt zone status does not relieve the company from keeping proper books of account under the Companies Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A register of beneficial owners must be maintained at the registered office and filed with the Gibraltar Companies Registry each year on the anniversary of incorporation. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be recorded in the register and notified to the central database within 28 days. The annual confirmation verifies the accuracy of the register and identifies all movements during the preceding year. Non-compliance is a criminal offence carrying fines and director disqualification.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,500 – $4,000 (Gibraltar registered agent and registered office service for a Bermuda Exempted Company operating as a tax-exempt manufacturing entity)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $7,500 – $20,000 (Gibraltar independent audit firm for IFRS financial statements of a micro-mobility electric cargo bicycle manufacturer)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% — flat corporate income tax rate on chargeable profits under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended), applied identically to resident and non-resident companies that carry on a trade or derive income sourced in Gibraltar.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate for a qualifying non-resident exempted-status company holding passive investments: (i) central management and control exercised outside Gibraltar; (ii) no trade, permanent establishment or fixed base of business in Gibraltar; (iii) no Gibraltar-source income. Additional statutory reliefs: Gibraltar participation exemption disregards dividends received from a qualifying subsidiary (shareholding of 10% or more held for at least 12 months); no tax on capital gains realised on disposal of shares or other capital assets; foreign-source income not attributable to a Gibraltar activity remains outside the charge. However, any manufacturing, assembly, warehousing or distribution activity physically conducted in Gibraltar is fully chargeable at the 12.5% headline rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Company Income Tax Return — Form CAT/SC (Corporation Tax Self-Assessment), issued by the Commissioner of Income Tax under section 12 of the Income Tax Act 2010; submitted electronically through the Gibraltar Income Tax Office eTax electronic filing portal, or physically at the Income Tax Office, Europort, Gibraltar.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual — one return per chargeable period (accounting period); a nil return is mandatory even where the exempted company has zero chargeable profits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be delivered within 12 months after the end of the accounting period (chargeable period), unless the Commissioner notifies an earlier date; a final self-assessment and any corporation tax payment at 12.5% fall due on the same date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name, Gibraltar Companies Registry number, date of incorporation and principal registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as per the Gibraltar Companies Registry certificate. For an exempted-status non-resident company, append the notation 'Non-resident — managed and controlled outside Gibraltar' and attach the certificate of non-residence or exempted-status confirmation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the accounting period covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the accounting period elected by board resolution or adopted in the articles. Any change of accounting reference date must be notified to the Commissioner and the Registrar of Companies before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profits of any trade or business carried on in Gibraltar, adjusted for allowable deductions, capital allowances and prior-year loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'NIL' where no trade, permanent establishment or fixed base of business exists in Gibraltar. If any physical e-bike assembly, quality control, warehousing or B2B sales activity is conducted in Gibraltar, all attributable profit must be declared here and is chargeable at 12.5%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income arising outside Gibraltar, including dividends, interest, royalties, foreign branch profits and capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure holding exempted company may exclude qualifying foreign dividends and passive income. Attach the participation-exemption election and evidence of beneficial ownership of the underlying shareholdings. Income economically sourced in Gibraltar cannot be re-characterised as foreign merely by routing payments through an offshore bank account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred wholly and exclusively for the Gibraltar trade, statutory capital allowances, and brought-forward loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim loss relief strictly within the 5-year carryforward limit. Intercompany management fees, royalties and service charges must be substantiated by an OECD-aligned transfer pricing file; otherwise deductions are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net adjusted chargeable profit after all exemptions, deductions and loss relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a qualifying non-resident exempted company holding only passive assets, enter '0'. Where any Gibraltar-source profit exists, that amount is taxable and may not be reduced by artificial allocation to an overseas board of directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at the statutory rate of 12.5% on the chargeable profit, less payments on account or tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute 12.5% only on genuine Gibraltar-source chargeable profits. No deemed exemption, notional credit or exempted-status carve-out applies to Gibraltar-source trading profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed declaration by a director or appointed Gibraltar tax representative attesting to the accuracy, completeness and truthfulness of the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Appoint a Gibraltar tax representative holding a power of attorney for filing and correspondence. Non-resident directors remain criminally liable for false declarations; signature by a third-party service provider does not transfer tax liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of £100 per chargeable period; daily default penalties of £50 per day for each day the return remains outstanding after 90 days, accumulating until compliance. Inaccurate, negligent or fraudulent returns attract tax-geared penalties of up to 100% of the understated tax plus statutory late-payment interest under section 100 of the Income Tax Act 2010. Criminal prosecution may add further fines and imprisonment. Persistent default by a non-resident company can trigger loss of non-resident status and reassessment on a worldwide basis.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid by a Gibraltar company to non-resident shareholders, whether final, interim or in-kind distributions. No deduction at source, advance corporation tax or qualifying holding period applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the statutory rate is 0%, no Gibraltar withholding tax reclaim is required on outbound distributions. Protocol to substantiate foreign tax treaty benefits: (i) file Tax Residency Certificate application Form TRC-CO with the Commissioner of Income Tax, enclosing the consolidated Certificate of Incorporation, audited accounts, board minutes evidencing management-and-control location, the Gibraltar Register of Beneficial Owners extract, and confirmation of exempted/non-resident status or economic substance compliance; (ii) obtain the TRC (usual administrative service standard 5–10 business days); (iii) apostille the TRC and file it with the foreign revenue authority together with the applicable treaty relief form (for the United Kingdom, HMRC Form DT-Gibraltar referencing the UK–Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement signed 27 March 2019, effective for Gibraltar taxes from 1 January 2019 and UK taxes from 1 January 2020); (iv) establish beneficial ownership of the dividend and absence of a principal purpose of treaty abuse under the OECD Principal Purpose Test and any Limitation-on-Benefits clause. Gibraltar's wider double tax treaty network remains limited; professionals must confirm the specific treaty in force for each shareholder jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% on outbound royalty and interest payments made by a Gibraltar company. Treaty rate: 0% for interest and royalties under the UK–Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and, for IP royalties, the arrangement satisfies the associated-enterprises and genuine economic substance conditions. The payer retains deductibility only for arm's-length, contemporaneously documented arrangements supported by a transfer pricing file.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP 1,000,000 (approximately GBP 1,000,000) aggregate value of controlled transactions per chargeable period triggers mandatory Local File preparation. A combined Master File and Local File is required where Gibraltar-resident turnover exceeds GIP 20,000,000. Country-by-Country reporting applies to multinational groups whose consolidated group revenue is at least EUR 750,000,000, with the Gibraltar constituent entity designated as the filing entity or surrogate filer.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Gibraltar applies a mandatory economic substance regime aligned with OECD and EU standards, enacted through the Income Tax Act 2010 and the Gibraltar Economic Substance (Income Tax) Regulations 2019 (GRES). A company conducting a relevant activity — banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, distribution, service centre, or pure equity holding — must demonstrate: (i) direction and management in Gibraltar evidenced by board meetings held in Gibraltar, quorum, minutes and substantive decision-making; (ii) physical premises proportionate to activity; (iii) full-time employees commensurate with core income-generating activities; and (iv) performance of core income-generating activities in Gibraltar. A pure equity holding company benefits from a reduced substance test: registered office, one director, one shareholder, and timely filing of accounts and returns. An exempted-status manufacturing company claiming non-residence must evidence at least one substantive CIGA in Gibraltar (for example, procurement, assembly supervision, quality control or contract manufacturing management); failure to do so creates UK/Gibraltar tax-residency risk under the management-and-control test and exposes the entity to reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Filing (Income Tax Act 2010; Crimes Act 2011, Part 16)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a nil CAT/SC return while deriving Gibraltar-source profits from the assembly, storage or B2B distribution of electric cargo e-bikes; destroying or falsifying purchase invoices, bills of lading or payment records; using a non-resident nominee board to conceal actual management exercised in Gibraltar or the United Kingdom; failing to disclose physical presence of key personnel in Gibraltar exercising operational control; and deliberately mischaracterising manufacturing service fees as foreign passive income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: tax-geared penalty of up to 100% of the understated tax, statutory interest, and best-of-judgment assessments. Criminal: fraudulent evasion of income tax carries up to 7 years' imprisonment; general fraud under the Crimes Act 2011 carries up to 14 years' imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine; forfeiture of assets derived from evasion is ordered under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate veil where the exempted company is a mere façade or instrumentality of fraud; directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded tax and civil penalties, subject to disqualification orders of up to 15 years under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, travel restraint orders pending criminal trial, confiscation and Serious Crime Prevention Orders, and imprisonment on conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Non-Compliance (GRES Regulations 2019; Income Tax Act 2010)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a brass-plate Gibraltar office with no local employees, no board meetings and no substantive decision-making while claiming exempted/non-resident status; routing e-bike OEM purchase and assembly payments through Gibraltar as pass-through invoices without a CUP, TNMM or profit-split allocation; failing to file the annual GRES economic substance self-declaration; and deriving distribution or headquarters income without proportionate premises and staff in Gibraltar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at 12.5% with attribution of deemed Gibraltar-source profit; administrative economic substance penalties of up to GIP 100,000 per period; forced registration as a Gibraltar tax-resident company; strike-off and dissolution under the Companies Act 2014; enhanced information exchange under Gibraltar's Tax Information Exchange Agreements; and referral of the file to the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit for money-laundering review.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered personally to discharge the company's reassessed tax and penalties where they knowingly permitted the substance failure. Directors face disqualification for up to 15 years, personal liability for fraudulent trading under the Companies Act 2014 (civil liability for the full amount of debts incurred during the substance-deficient period), and, in egregious cases, travel bans pending criminal investigation for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Financial Crime (Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; Criminal Justice (Money Laundering) Regulations 2016)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Swift/TT wire transfers or LC payments for e-bike orders routed through the exempted company from high-risk jurisdictions without completing customer due diligence on B2B dealers; structuring transactions to avoid the GIP 15,000 threshold reporting obligations; converting customer deposits into shareholder loans or equity to disguise criminal proceeds; failing to file Suspicious Activity Reports with the Gibraltar Financial Intelligence Unit; and handling crypto-currency settlements without a corresponding custody or payment-services licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: On indictment: imprisonment for up to 14 years and/or an unlimited fine; confiscation of the proceeds under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015; civil forfeiture; administrative monetary penalties of up to GIP 2,500,000 imposed by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission; and revocation of corporate service provider, EMI or banking arrangements, resulting in loss of the payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are personally liable where the corporate veil is pierced for money-laundering activity; courts may issue travel bans, impose Serious Crime Prevention Orders, order disqualification from directorship for up to 15 years, require disgorgement of laundered profits, and authorise extradition to the United Kingdom or EU member states under Gibraltar–UK and Gibraltar–EU cooperation instruments.
